findings.title: Segment size and span-count guard removed, so oversized segments are no longer rejected
findings.body: The diff removes the `max_segment_spans` check in `_load_segment_data` (the 'segment_span_count_exceeded' branch) entirely, while the constructor still accepts and stores `max_segment_spans`. The byte-size check remains, but the span-count limit that protected the flusher from huge segments is gone and the parameter is now dead. Segments with more spans than the configured limit will be loaded and flushed instead of skipped, which changes flush behavior without any stated reason.

findings.title: zpopmin trims the segment to 1000 but the sorted-set score is end timestamp, and span_count after zunionstore may be stale
findings.body: `span_count` is only set from zunionstore when a merge happens; when no merge occurs but the set already exists, `zcard` is used, which is fine. However when a merge happens, zunionstore returns the union size, and then `zpopmin` removes the lowest-scored (oldest-ending) spans, silently dropping spans from the segment on every insert once above 1000 spans. Dropped spans are data loss with no metric or log, and the eviction policy (oldest end timestamp) is not documented or tested.

findings.title: zadd with payload as member collapses identical payloads and uses end timestamp as score
findings.body: Switching from sadd to zadd keys members by the raw payload bytes. Duplicate span payloads now collapse silently (same as before), but the score is the span's end_timestamp_precise, and in `process_spans` the zadd is done in a separate pipeline before the Lua call, so a re-delivered span with a changed timestamp overwrites the score. Combined with eviction by lowest score, this can evict the wrong spans. Behavior is not covered by tests.

findings.title: Missing end_timestamp_precise key raises KeyError for every span
findings.body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` is indexed directly, so any span event lacking this field (older Relay versions or malformed payloads) now raises KeyError and fails the whole batch, whereas previously such spans were processed. The cast to SpanEvent also does not validate anything at runtime.

findings.title: Negative offsets are now passed to the queryset in BasePaginator, causing wrong results
findings.body: The change to `get_result` replaces `queryset[offset:stop]` with `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`. For is_prev cursors a negative offset is passed straight to slicing, which Django rejects (ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported) and for next cursors negative offsets are silently clamped, hiding the cursor's offset. Behavior of every existing paginator subclass changes.

findings.title: Advanced-feature path allows arbitrary negative offsets to read beyond pagination bounds
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator honors any negative cursor.offset when enable_advanced_features is set, slicing the queryset with negative indices. Negative slicing on a Django queryset fetches from the end and bypasses the normal pagination window; the comment claims permissions are checked at the queryset level, but the queryset is just the caller's filtered audit log queryset, so this exposes arbitrary rows ordering-wise. The gate is only superuser or global access, which is a broad, unreviewed data-access expansion.

findings.title: Undocumented optimized_pagination query flag switches paginator and enables negative offsets
findings.body: A new `optimized_pagination=true` request parameter selects OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features for superusers/global-access members. This is an unannounced API surface, introduced in an endpoint publicly marked EXPERIMENTAL, with behavior that is not tested and not described anywhere. The `enable_advanced` check also reads `request.user.is_superuser` on an endpoint that already has permission checks, so the gate is ad hoc.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offset support that the cursor does not implement
findings.body: The added comment says the Cursor enables efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions, but Cursor only stores int(offset) and has no logic for negative offsets; the claim is misleading for maintainers and describes behavior the change doesn't deliver.

findings.title: Lua loop bound and eviction limit are magic numbers that disagree with the constructor default
findings.body: add-buffer.lua now hard-codes 1000 for the redirect loop and the eviction cap, while the Python constructor default `max_segment_spans` is 1001 and is no longer enforced. The three values are inconsistent and the Lua limit is not configurable, so the Python setting has no effect on the actual cap.

findings.title: No tests cover the new eviction, zunionstore merge, or negative-offset paths
findings.body: The tests only add end_timestamp_precise to existing fixtures. Nothing exercises the >1000 span eviction in add-buffer.lua, the zset-based merging, or the OptimizedCursorPaginator / negative-offset behavior, so the regressions above would go undetected.
